written: before the amended instrument run; the initial-rule run and its report are preserved byte-for-byte (report.v1-initial-rule.json sha256 d2f3f8cc91a8e0de8a27e58a9ea7649feb426d76504393821eb49b447b5cba3e)

observed_in_initial_run.root_cause: R4's title test was too literal for two legitimate bibliographic variants: (a) SRC-086 (Crossref) drops the subtitle 'The interior of the black hole region' present in SRC-057, so token Jaccard = 0.70; (b) SRC-024 spells 'spacetimes' where SRC-087 spells 'space-times', so hyphen-stripping produced 'space times' vs 'spacetimes' and Jaccard = 0.82. Both pairs share the same arXiv id, so the identifier link is not in question; only the MERGE-vs-LINK decision needs the title test.

changed_clause.new_R4_title_agreement: normalized-title equality, OR compact-form equality (all non-alphanumerics removed, so 'space-times' == 'spacetimes'), OR token Jaccard >= 0.90, OR (both titles >= 8 tokens AND the shorter token sequence is a contiguous prefix of the longer). Everything else is unchanged: a mirror edge still fails on title disagreement, and |year_i - year_j| > 4 still marks it SUSPECT.

effect_predictions_after_amendment.A1: SRC-086/SRC-057 and SRC-087/SRC-024 become title-consistent, their mirror edges stop being suspect, and P7 = 7 LINK_ONLY
effect_predictions_after_amendment.A2: SRC-093 -> SRC-033 stays SUSPECT (different works, not a prefix/subset, and year gap 2009 vs 2018 > 4)
effect_predictions_after_amendment.A3: no MERGE_DUPLICATE disposition changes; in particular the three merge groups and the four superseded rows of the initial run are unchanged
effect_predictions_after_amendment.A4: controls C2-C7 and predictions P1-P6 still hold
